_strings.@@0d406d0f29b1: Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit — Available only to a person who received a 2025 Volunteer Emergency Worker Credit Certificate from IDOR. Includes volunteers registered with the Illinois Emergency Management Agency (IEMA) and Office of Homeland Security (OHS) who volunteered at least 100 hours during the immediately preceding calendar year, in addition to non-full-time fire department/fire protection district/fire protection association volunteers. Must have served as a volunteer emergency worker at least 9 months during the taxable year, not receive more than $5,000 in compensation for those services, apply with IDOR, and be one of the first 10,000 qualified applicants. Note: the income limit that applies to the property tax / K-12 credits does NOT apply to this credit.
_strings.@@0f330f00ff9e: Treaty conformity — IL conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IL income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IL return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: IL-1040 starts from federal adjusted gross income: the 2025 IL-1040 face, Step 2 Line 1, prints "Federal adjusted gross income from your federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR, Line 11a", and the 2025 Instructions' Step 2 Line 1 read "Adjusted gross income — Enter the adjusted gross income from your federal return." The instructions ("What is Illinois income?") confirm "Your Illinois income includes the adjusted gross income (AGI) amount figured on your federal return, plus any additional income that must be added to your AGI." Income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. income tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI, so it flows through and is not re-taxed. Illinois additions are limited: Line 2 "Federally tax-exempt income" applies ONLY to federally tax-exempt interest and dividend income reported on federal Form 1040 Line 2a (municipal bond interest), not to foreign treaty income; Line 3/Schedule M "Other additions" enumerates specific items (child's 8814 interest/dividends, pass-through additions, Section 529/ABLE earnings, IL-4562 special depreciation, business expense recapture, etc.) and contains no add-back of federal income-tax-treaty-exempt income. There is NO California-style Schedule CA treaty addback. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and IL conforms.
_strings.@@10b0394b539d: 2025 Form IL-1040 Instructions (PDF title "2025 IL-1040 Instructions, Illinois Individual Income Tax"; internal label "IL-1040 Instructions (R-02/25)") — What''s New for 2025 / cover / mailing addresses, due date (April 15, 2026), income tax rate ("The Illinois income tax rate is 4.95 percent (.0495)"), exemption allowance ("The personal exemption amount for tax year 2025 is $2,850")
_strings.@@1acafbca8a88: Illinois Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) — In general, anyone who qualified for the federal EITC also qualifies for the Illinois EITC. Eligibility is expanded beyond the federal qualifications: taxpayers who meet all federal EITC qualifications EXCEPT that they file with an IRS-issued ITIN (no valid SSN required for taxpayer, spouse, or qualifying children), and/or are age 18-24 or 65+ with no qualifying child, may also claim it. Must have earned income under the federal limits in Table 1, investment income below $11,950, not have filed federal Form 2555, and meet the other federal EITC rules.

Not available for mobile home privilege tax, penalties/fees, property outside Illinois, or the portion of property tax deductible as a business expense. Nonresidents may not take this credit.

_strings.@@adbea73c1187: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): Illinois Child Tax Credit INCREASED to 40% of the Illinois Earned Income Tax Credit for 2025, up from 20% for 2024 (What's New for 2025: "Illinois Child Tax Credit amount was increased to 40 percent of the Illinois Earned Income Tax Credit"). The 2025 Schedule IL-E/EITC Step 5, Line 12 prints "Multiply the amount on Line 11 [the Illinois EITC from Line 9] by 40% (0.4). This is your Illinois Child Tax Credit." Eligibility is unchanged (qualify for the Illinois EITC and have at least one dependent child under age 12 as of the last day of 2025); the credit stays refundable. Pack notes: Dependent exemptions (Line 10d) ship for 2025 at $2,850 each: the 2025 Schedule IL-E/EITC form prints the per-dependent multiplication (Step 2 Line 1, $2,850 per dependent), so dependents_count is applied at $2,850 each. Exemption phase-out: the entire Line 10 exemption allowance (including Lines 10b-10d) is $0 when federal AGI exceeds $500,000 (married filing jointly) or $250,000 (all other statuses) — the 'Income Exceptions' box in the Line 10 instructions / Exemption Allowance Chart. Claimed as a dependent by another: if base income exceeds $2,850, the filer's own exemption is $0 (Line 10a chart rows with the Step 1 Line C box checked). Rate is UNCHANGED at 4.95% (.0495) for 2025; the exemption amount is year-specific ($2,850 for 2025, $2,775 for 2024) — never carry an exemption amount to another year.
